question_vi: @Valid và @Validated trong Spring Boot khác nhau thế nào?
question_en: How do @Valid and @Validated differ in Spring Boot?
answer_html_vi:
Cả 2 trigger Bean Validation trên method argument hoặc field.

@Valid (Jakarta)@Validated (Spring)
Validation groupsKhôngCó
Method-level validationKhôngCó — (đặt class level)

Cơ bản (dùng cái nào cũng được): create(@RequestBody @Valid CreateUserRequest req).

Khác biệt thực sự — validation groups:

java
interface OnCreate {}  interface OnUpdate {}

record UserRequest(
  @Null(groups = OnCreate.class) @NotNull(groups = OnUpdate.class) Long id,
  @NotBlank String name
) {}

@PostMapping ResponseEntity<User> create(@RequestBody @Validated(OnCreate.class) UserRequest req) {}
@PutMapping  ResponseEntity<User> update(@RequestBody @Validated(OnUpdate.class) UserRequest req) {}

Cùng 1 DTO, rule khác nhau theo ngữ cảnh (create: id phải null; update: id bắt buộc).

@Validated đặt trên class còn bật validate tham số method thường: find(@NotNull @Positive Long id).

Validation fail → MethodArgumentNotValidException → bắt bằng @ExceptionHandler (xem câu @ControllerAdvice).
answer_html_en:
Both trigger Bean Validation on method arguments or fields.

@Valid (Jakarta)@Validated (Spring)
Validation groupsNoYes
Method-level validationNoYes — (class level)

Basic usage (either works): create(@RequestBody @Valid CreateUserRequest req).

The real difference — validation groups:

java
interface OnCreate {}  interface OnUpdate {}

record UserRequest(
  @Null(groups = OnCreate.class) @NotNull(groups = OnUpdate.class) Long id,
  @NotBlank String name
) {}

@PostMapping ResponseEntity<User> create(@RequestBody @Validated(OnCreate.class) UserRequest req) {}
@PutMapping  ResponseEntity<User> update(@RequestBody @Validated(OnUpdate.class) UserRequest req) {}

One DTO, different rules per context (create: id must be null; update: id required).

@Validated on a class also enables validating plain method params: find(@NotNull @Positive Long id).

Validation failure → MethodArgumentNotValidException → catch with @ExceptionHandler (see the @ControllerAdvice item).
